tossups.text: This structure is the defining characteristic separating the fish in subclass Dipnoi ["dip-NOH-eye"] from all other extant species of Sarcopterygii ["sar-cop-TARE-uh-jee"]. Although it is evolutionarily unrelated to this structure, arachnids possess stacks of hemolymph-filled tissue known as the "book" form of this organ. This organ in terrestrial mammals is homologous to the swim bladders used by many species of fish to control buoyancy. In humans, its parenchymal ["pah-REN-kuh-mull"] tissue contains hollow cavities called alveoli, which are connected to bronchioles. For 10 points, name this vital organ that conducts the function of gas exchange within land-dwelling vertebrates.

This element can be transferred from water to toluene by using TOAB as a phase-transfer agent in the Brust-Schiffrin method, while adding small amounts of sodium citrate is used in a similar method for this element that was first employed by Turkevich. Relativistic contractions in this element's s orbitals shifts them closer to its d orbitals, causing it to absorb blue light in a manner similar to cesium. At one point, liquid mercury was used to extract this metal from ores, but it is now mostly extracted through cyanide leaching. It's not platinum, but this metal is often refined using a mixture of hydrochloric and nitric acid called aqua regia. An alternate name for iron pyrite comes from the fact that it resembles this element. For 10 points, name this metal found below silver in the periodic table, which has atomic symbol Au.

One model of his theories plots national income against the interest rate and was developed by John R. Hicks and presented in a paper called this man "and the Classics: A Suggested Interpretation." This thinker gives his name to a graphical representation of an intersection between a consumption function of consumers and the aggregate demand function. This man wrote a book analyzing the economic impact of the Treaty of Versailles, called The Economic Consequences of the Peace. Paul Krugman has called for a return to this man's principles. For 10 points, name this British economist, an advocate of government spending, and author of The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money.

A group of people was subjected to this event due to the Treaty of New Echota. Present-day Oklahoma, then a territory, was the destination for many victims of this event, which got its name from the oppression of the Cherokee nation during it. Andrew Jackson supported, for ten points, what nineteenth century event in which tribes of Native Americans were forcibly relocated west of the Mississippi River?

As he observes these animals in battle, the speaker of a poem notes that "these storms of passion, these conflicts so fierce, by the tossing of a little dust are quelled and laid to rest." The only extended simile in Works and Days compares idleness to the behavior of one type of these animals. In the Homeric Hymn to Hermes, Apollo tells the young god that he can acquire the gift of prophecy from three goddesses described as these animals. The fourth book of a poem relates that Jupiter blessed these animals for feeding him in Dicte's cave. Ancient depictions of these animals sometimes describe them being spontaneously generated from the corpses of cattle in a process called bugonia. The various Greek tribes are compared to groups of these animals emerging from rocks in the very first Homeric simile of the Iliad, and Virgil's second simile in the Aeneid describes the Tyrians building Carthage as akin to these animals. For 10 points, name these animals kept by Aristaeus in the Georgics, whose last section concerns the restoration of their hives.

A theory that opposes this theory claims that people infer their attitudes from observing their behavior the same way an outside observer would. Daryl Bem's self-perception theory opposes this phenomenon, which one study attributed to "forced compliance." A community of UFO cultists dealing with the effects of this phenomenon is analyzed in When Prophecy Fails, which was written by a psychologist who tested this phenomenon by offering students either one or twenty dollars to perform boring tasks. For 10 points, name this phenomenon that was described by Leon Festinger, in which people experience discomfort when they try to reconcile contradictory beliefs.

Standing in Kluane National Park, it was first climbed in 1925 by an expedition led by Albert MacCarthy. . Rising from the St. Elias mountains, it reaches a height of 17,224 feet over the Mentasta Pass. In 2005, Jean Chretien proposed that it be renamed after Pierre Trudeau, but after a backlash from geologists it was left bearing the name of the founder of the Canadian Geological Survey. For 10 points, name this highest mountain of Canada.

this structure is essential for bronchi and bronchioles. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in bronchi and bronchioles.

tossups.text: This conflict sparked leaders on the losing side to form the Syndicate to work out the impending crisis of political succession. Following this conflict, thousands of citizens were interred in Deoli. During this war in which the Forward Policy was used, the commander B. M. Kaul developed pleurisy and had to leave the front. This war violated the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence signed 8 years earlier. Early operations in this war included an attack on Namka Chu and the seizing of Tawang, and it resulted in an exchange of high-altitude territory across the McMahon Line. Tensions between the two adversaries in this conflict escalated a few years before when one agreed to shelter the Dalai Lama. For 10 points, name this 1962 border conflict between the world's two most populous countries.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for parathyroid hormone. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this thyroid-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The thyroid is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in parathyroid hormone.

tossups.text: One of these musical entities named for the city of Naples can serve as a predominant. One of these musical entities denoted by the Roman numeral "V" often leads to one of these entities labeled "I." Types of these musical entities include major, minor, diminished, and augmented. Guitarists and pianists often play these musical entities as accompaniment for vocalists. For 10 points, name these musical entities consisting of multiple notes that sound simultaneously.

Its "New Classical" form can be derived from the Lucas supply function, and Robert Gordon has developed a 'Triangle Model' which takes cost push, supply shocks, and other factors into account to modify it. Blanchard and Gali have written on the 'New Keynesian' variety of it, and it can be theoretically derived from Okun's Law. It was first explicitly shown to hold in the United States by Paul Samuelson and Robert Solow, but it could not explain stagflation until Edmund Phelps and Milton Friedman showed that it is vertical in the long-run. For 10 points, identify this graph which shows the trade-off between unemployment and inflation, named for a New Zealand economist.

Proponents of this economist's theories argue against Say's law. Aggregate supply and aggregate demand are plotted on the x and y axis of his namesake "cross." This man criticized the Treaty of Versailles and argued against war reparations in The Economic Consequences of the Peace, and wrote The General Theory of Employment. His ideas are often contrasted with supply-side economics. For 10 points, name this British economist who supported stimulus spending.

This character travels from Trondheim to Lusitania, where he meets the alien "piggies" who die and become trees. The original book featuring this character is set 3,000 years earlier on an Earth governed by Starways Congress. This protagonist of a book series was born due to the failure of his older siblings to be accepted into Battle School. For 10 points, name this character who commits xenocide on the "bugger" race in a novel by Orson Scott Card.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on Speaker for the Dead

tossups.text: Dahm and Scalapino extended the nonlinear form of this effect to IMD power and harmonic generation, while an alternative approach was devised by Agassi and Oates. It can be obtained from taking the curl of the Proca equations, and can be understood through the Anderson-Higgs mechanism. The degree to which it is performed is known as the London penetration depth, and Svedlindh discovered that a positive susceptibility is found in materials displaying the anti-variety of this effect, which is sometimes known as the Wohlleben effect. It can occur completely when a screening current is induced on the surface of a certain kind of "soft" material in such a direction as to exactly cancel the external field within the material, and it was discovered by its namesake along with Robert Ochsenfeld. For 10 points, name this effect in which superconductors lose their magnetism.

This statement can be used to explain the teapot effect, while it is often incorrectly used to explain airfoil lift in the equal transit-time explanation. One application of this concept describes how pressure drops as a fluid flows through a narrow section of a pipe and is named for Venturi. Integrating the Euler equations gives a form of this equation that is true for unsteady flows. This relation states that the sum of volume squared over 2, the gravitational force, and pressure over density is constant for incompressible flows. For 10 points, name this principle that associates a decrease in a fluid's static pressure with an increase in its speed.

Surviving studies for the work show that two men, a student and a seated sailor, were originally meant to have been included in this painting. A thin strip of shades of brown appears on the left, but more disconcerting is the wedge of melon, bunch of grapes, and other pieces of fruit that are out of place at the bottom center. The final word in its title refers, surprisingly, to a red-light district in whose prostitutes inspired this 1907 work. Often considered the earliest Cubist work, For 10 points, name this depiction of five female nudes and first masterpiece of Pablo Picasso.

One poem in this language addresses a figure who "like the stab of a knife, entered my plaintive heart." A poem in this language describes how men trap creatures whose "great white wings / drag beside them like oars." The title figure of one poem in this language is described as a "prince of cloud and sky."A poetry collection written in this language often mentions the concept of "Ennui" ("on-WEE"). A section of a work in this language titled "Spleen and Ideal" contains the poem "The Albatross." A collection in this language addresses a "hypocrite reader" and is titled The Flowers of Evil. For 10 points, name this language used by poets like Charles Baudelaire.

In the process of crafting a deterministic linear-time algorithm to construct these objects, which has a runtime proportional to the inverse Ackermann function, Bernard Chazelle invented the soft heap. The verification step from Boruvka's algorithm for finding these objects is sometimes used in other algorithms for them. Because the set of forests of a graph forms a graphic matroid, greedy algorithms are very effective at constructing these objects. Constructing one of these objects often relies on finding a light edge that crosses a cut. Two algorithms used to find these objects, which run in big O of edges times log of vertices, are Kruskal's algorithm and Prim's algorithm. For 10 points, name these acyclic subgraphs that connect all the vertices of a graph, with smallest edge cost.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for major veins (vena cava, jugular, portal). It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this aorta-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The aorta is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in major veins (vena cava, jugular, portal).

parts.text: Name this technique for analyzing an algorithm's runtime in which one averages over a worst-case sequence of operations. Hence, it is concerned with the actual runtime.

Robert Tarjan introduced amortized analysis as a formal method and developed a wide array of data structures. With Daniel Sleator, Tarjan created splay trees, which are self-adjusting examples of the "search" type of these trees.
As amortized analysis gives an upper bound on an algorithm's run time, it uses this notation. A less common alternative is big Omega, which gives an asymptotic lower bound.

bonuses.leadin: The three most common types of this technique are aggregate analysis, the accounting method, and the potential method. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify these places that Thorstein Veblen said were dominated by business interests in America. Among the findings of the report A Nation at Risk was that Americans were being inadequately prepared for these places.
acceptableAnswers: prompt on institutions of higher learning

parts.text: Bok analyzed the social responsibilities of the university in a work titled "Beyond" this structure. This two-word metaphor is named for a precious material that elephants are hunted for.

A long-time UCLA scholar with this surname wrote the international study The Higher Education System, which applied Erving Goffman's concept of "cooling out" to higher education. This is also the first name of the author of The Uses of the University.

bonuses.leadin: Most of Derek Bok's work concerns the industry dominated by these places, including his 2007 book that called these places "underachieving." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this legal process in which lenders recover the amount owed on a defaulted loan, leading to the seizure of one's home.

In a foreclosure, a termination of the borrower's equitable right of redemption is obtained by a "holder" named for this term. This term refers to a legal claim against assets used as collateral to repay debt.
In some foreclosures, the owner fails to comply with a lender-borrower agreement named for one of these things "of trust." These signed legal documents transfer ownership of an asset to a new owner.

bonuses.leadin: Amid a 2010s crisis, Bank of America and other banks put a freeze on instances of this action. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this series of two wars fought between British settlers and the namesake Dutch-speaking settlers in South Africa.
The Jameson Raid was an attempt to take over this largest city in South Africa.
One supporter of the Jameson Raid was this diamond magnate, who dreamed of a Cape-to-Cairo railway and established a scholarship for foreigners to study at Oxford.

bonuses.leadin: These wars included the Jameson Raid and the Siege of Mafeking. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author who wrote about Marie de France in her 2021 novel Matrix. The marriage of the Broadway writer Lotto Satterwhite and Mathilde Yoder is the subject of this author's Fates and Furies.
In Groff's The Monsters of Templeton, a 50-foot creature turns up dead in a lake with this name. Hurry Harry explains this other name for Otsego Lake to Natty Bumppo in The Deerslayer.

Groff's novel with this title is about a utopian commune in upstate New York. The hermit of Sidley Park turns out to be Thomasina Coverly's tutor Septimus Hodge in Tom Stoppard's play with this title.

bonuses.leadin: In a novel by this author, the protagonist decides to build a labyrinth between her abbey and the town after she has a vision of the Virgin Mary surrounded by swirling rose petals. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these non-consonantal sounds of language which are categorized by roundness, tenseness, and tongue location. In English, they underwent a "Great Shift" between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries.
This term is given to a gliding transition between two vowels in the same syllable, and can be found in words like "boy" or "write."

This nineteenth-century German linguist, a frequent collaborator with brother Wilhelm, names a law that formalizes relations between stops and fricatives in Proto-Germanic, a chain shift similar to the Great Vowel Shift.

bonuses.leadin: Otto Jespersen studied a change in these sounds that exemplifies a chain shift. For 10 points each:

The highest mountain in the Rockies is this peak in central Colorado.
Running along the Rockies is this division which separates watersheds that drain west to the Pacific from those that drain east to the Atlantic.

bonuses.leadin: The Tetons of Wyoming are a sub-range of this mountain range. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Hans Scholl and Alexander Schmorell were among the members of this group of Munich-based students who distributed anti-Nazi leaflets throughout Germany. The philosophy professor Kurt Huber was also a member of this group.

One of only two people to receive honorary U.S. citizenship, this Swedish diplomat saved thousands of Jews by organizing protected houses in neutral countries. He disappeared after being taken prisoner by the Soviets in 1945.
This large Polish city was the site of a failed 1943 Jewish uprising crushed by Jurgen Stroop, and a subsquent general resistance against Nazi occupation of Poland.

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about people who resisted the Nazis, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with nasal cavity and sinuses.

parts.text: Name this American photographer who created One Nation, Indivisible and Migrant Mother.

Dorothea Lange's photograph Migrant Mother showcases the struggles of working-class Americans during this historical period. Lange's picture A Sign of the Times shows the heavily-mended stockings of a stenographer who couldn't afford new clothes during this extreme economic downturn.

Lange's One Nation, Indivisible, which shows schoolchildren reciting the Pledge of Allegiance, protested the forced relocation of American citizens to these institutions in the 1940s. Many of Lange's photographs were taken at Manzanar, one of these institutions created to house Americans of Japanese descent in California.

bonuses.leadin: This artist turned her attention to exposing social injustice after taking her camera down to the street near her New York apartment and photographing a bread line on a whim. For 10 points each,

parts.text: This type of society is characterised by the rule of women and inheritance through the female line, as opposed to societies where men rule.

Although later digs suggest otherwise, James Mellaart's excavation of this archaeological site in modern-day Turkey showed evidence of a matriarchal society. This Neolithic city was the most populous in the world around 6500 BCE.

In a 2022 book, Joan Marie Cichon argues that the presence of a Mother Goddess in civilizations on this island supports the theory of matriarchy during the Bronze Age. Arthur Evans became famous during the early 20th century for his work on this Mediterranean island.

bonuses.leadin: Marija Gimbutas [GIM-bu-tahs, hard G] coined the term "Old European" to describe a culture with this social structure that pre-dated the Proto-Indo-European culture. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this social science, the study of language.

Linguists often study the historical development of a language, from a simplified ¨pidgin¨stage, to this more stable stage of a mixed language that can be learned natively by children, and further into varieties, dialects, and languages. This term is also used to described racially-mixed ethnic groups, such as descendants of French settlers in Louisiana.

Linguists have not come to a complete consensus on whether this variety of English evolved from an African creole or an English creole. Linguists do not generally use the controversial term ¨Ebonics¨for this variety.

bonuses.leadin: Scholars within this field may focus on pragmatics, in which the context of a message is studied, on semantics, in which the meaning of words or symbols are studied, and/or on syntax, in which the structure of sentences are studied. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this Heian period story about the title Prince's rise from commoner status, often regarded as the world's first novel.
The Tale of Genji was written by this writer, who also appears in the novel as one of Prince Genji's love interests.
This Englishman's many translations include a six-volume translation of The Tale of Genji, which was published during the early 20th century.

bonuses.leadin: In this work, the title figure is forced to live in Suma for several years due to his amorous affairs causing scandal in the court. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this four-membered cyclic amide. This moiety is the active part of a namesake group of antibiotics that includes cephalosporins and penicillins.

This axially chiral compound was used as a chiral auxiliary in the synthesis of limonene. Many of its derivatives are also chiral auxiliaries or catalysts, including Shibasaki catalysts and ALB, as well as BINAP.

Synthesis of the Wieland-Miescher ketone uses this chiral organocatalyst that makes the aldol reaction asymmetric. The study of asymmetric organocatalysis began with this amino acid, whose catalytic activity is due to the secondary amine formed by its side chain looping around to connect to its amino group.

bonuses.leadin: An enantioselective synthesis of this moiety that combines an acyl chloride and an imine using proton sponge and a chiral cinchona alkaloid catalyst was developed by Lectka. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this class of blood cells. They generally have immune functions and are contrasted with red blood cells.
This class of lymphocytes (LIM-fuh-sites) develops in the bone marrow, and further differentiates into plasma cells and memory cells. These usually-CᐧDᐧ20-positive cells synthesize antibodies.

This kind of white blood cell binds to the IᐧgᐧE antibody. Cromolyn (KRAA-muh-lin) sodium stabilizes these cells, which like basophils (BAY-suh-fils) can degranulate and release histamine during hypersensitivity reactions.

bonuses.leadin: This class of cells can be divided into granulocytes (GRA-nyuh-loh-cites) and agranulocytes (ay-GRA-nyuh-loh-cites). For 10 points each:

parts.text: In the 2006 game Ōkami, a character named Issun accompanies and does the talking for this protagonist, who takes the form of a white wolf and is named for the sun goddess of the Shinto religion.

Claude is the silent protagonist of this sandbox game; in a later game in the series, Claude appears in a cameo, where he is still silent and described as "That mute asshole! That fucking snake without a tongue!"
The player character in Five Nights At Freddy's is also silent, even when the eponymous Freddy appears and plays a music-box version of this piece of classical music before killing him.

parts.text: Name this effect caused by a change in zero-point energy of a chemical bond due to the relative mass of different atoms.
The Kinetic Isotope effect is most notably observed when this isotope of hydrogen, containing one neutron, substitutes a proton.
Secondary kinetic isotope effects occur in reactions of this type, characterised by backside attack due to good overlap with the sigma antibonding orbital.
